source: CHGNet examples/fine_tuning.ipynb (CederGroupHub/chgnet): freeze the embeddings, basis expansions, atom_conv_layers[:-1], bond_conv_layers and angle_layers; StructureData with per-atom energies; get_train_val_test_loader(batch_size=8); Trainer(targets, optimizer='Adam', scheduler='CosLR', criterion='MSE', epochs=5, learning_rate=1e-2). Values below are the notebook's, unchanged, except targets (no stress / magmom labels exist here).

differences_from_the_notebook.targets: 'ef' not 'efsm': tstress is off in the C3b job format and there are no magnetic-moment labels
differences_from_the_notebook.split: explicit 90/10 train/valid files from the dataset stage; no test loader (the held-out sets are never given to the trainer)
differences_from_the_notebook.train_composition_model: false: the per-system energy reference is applied in the dataset stage (see scripts/finetune/data.py); the notebook offers train_composition_model=True or AtomRef.fit() for QE-scale energies, which at lr 1e-2 cannot move a per-element reference by ~10^3 eV in 5 epochs
differences_from_the_notebook.model_selection: the trainer's own bestE checkpoint: lowest VALIDATION energy MAE

epoch_budget_deviation: 2026-10-03, before any training data: budget raised from the documented 5 to 30 epochs (pre-registration Deviations D2). The documented value targets a different dataset size; at ~54 optimiser steps per epoch it would leave a refuted P1 indistinguishable from under-training. Selection stays on the validation split only (lowest validation loss); every other setting is the documented one.
